title: Healthcare Operations
subtitle: Earn trust through a narrow design-partner path under procurement, acceptance, and compliance pressure.
description: A painful healthcare workflow has real value, but users, champions, economic buyers, security, privacy, clinical operations, procurement, and authorized signatories operate on different timelines. Prove a narrow operational outcome without accepting unsafe delivery, data, service-level, payment, or liability obligations the startup cannot support.
learningObjectives: Map user, champion, buyer, privacy, security, and signatory authority
Use contractual boundaries to manage risk
Survive a long procurement and collection cycle
Distinguish signature from acceptance and cash

problems.title: Access depends on trust the founder has not earned
problems.summary: Workflow users cannot independently approve a pilot, data boundary, agreement, or production deployment.
hypotheses: An advisor can provide credible introductions
A non-clinical workflow avoids the access barrier
The initial institution is the wrong segment

problems.title: The data and regulatory boundary is undefined
problems.summary: A prototype or contract could create obligations the startup cannot support.
hypotheses: A manual process can avoid storing sensitive data

problems.title: Clinical value has no mapped economic buyer
problems.summary: User enthusiasm is disconnected from authority, budget, procurement timing, and acceptance criteria.
hypotheses: IT can sponsor a risk-reduction case
The labor saving is below the purchasing threshold

problems.title: The sales cycle is longer than personal runway
problems.summary: The founder needs learning-compatible income while navigating procurement and 60–120 day collection cycles.
hypotheses: A workflow audit can fund discovery
A smaller provider can move faster

problems.title: A signed design-partner agreement may still fail acceptance
problems.summary: Implementation dependencies, workflow safety, privacy evidence, and disputed acceptance can delay activation and cash while legal exposure grows.
hypotheses: A narrower non-clinical scope can pass acceptance
Milestone billing can share implementation risk
The first institution is too concentrated and demanding
